authority.note: This packet frames required adversarial reviews; script generation never answers or decides them.

limitations: Evidence context is assembled mechanically and may include irrelevant rows; the reviewer must judge relevance.
A pending red-team prompt is not a judgment_review and cannot support an M6 decision.
No script-authored verdict or recommendation is permitted.
Priority weights allocate review attention only.
Later judgment must preserve Commander-first identity and bracket-specific context.

reviews.adversarial_challenge: Assume multiple permanent types are answered over several turns. Identify which strategic routes actually rebuild and which collapse after repeated removal.

value: Don't convert into generic Grixis reanimator/control.
Don't force a cEDH shell; the plan is Demon density and power.

blueprint_failure_modes.description: Too many six- to eight-mana Demons: slow, dead hands.
Prince of Chaos and Demon drawbacks drain your own life.
Removal on a six-drop commander quickly becomes prohibitive.
mitigations: Spark Double and copies as backups

value.interaction: Counters for the big turn plus sweepers (Blasphemous Act, Toxic Deluge) to buy time.
value.mana: Rituals and rocks to reach six; 33-35 lands.
value.protection: Fierce Guardianship, Deflecting Swat; Be'lakor is six mana so recasting is costly.

accepted_role.advances_plan: Lord of Torment converts every Demon ETB into removal or face damage, and Prince of Chaos refuels; copies of Be'lakor (Spark Double, Rite of Replication) are the biggest turns.
accepted_role.honest_note: Six mana and needs other Demons; the draw costs life equal to cards drawn. Slow without ramp.

reviews.question: Can the deck rebuild after repeated removal across multiple permanent types?
